sources.citation: Maho, Jouni Filip. 2009. NUGL Online: the online version of the New Updated Guthrie List (version dated 4 June 2009).
sources.note: Classification only: K18 Nkangala nkn, in the K10 Ciokwe-Luchazi group beside K12b Ngangela/Nyemba, K13 Luchazi, K15 Mbunda, K17 Mbwela.

sources.citation: Bantu-languages.com (Jacky Maniacky), bibliographic database based on Glottolog 5.3 — queries sigle=K18 (Nkangala), ref_biblio=Nkangala, sigle=K12b (48 entries), K13, K15, K17, author=Fleisch.
sources.note: K18 Nkangala: '0 result found.. No results matched the search criteria.' The K12b (Ngangela/Nyemba) list surfaces the only cluster-level works: Fleisch 2008 (SUGIA 19) and Fleisch 2009 on the Ngangela-Nyemba dialect cluster, Lilunga 1981 'Elementos gramaticais da língua ngangela' (Menongue), Baião/Lecomte 1938-39 Ganguela grammar and dictionary (Cubango), Pearson 1970 Ngangela-English dictionary, Maniacky 2003, Zavoni 2003/2006 — none of them about Nkangala proper.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, languoid page Nkangala [nkan1238] (Hammarström et al. 2026). Glottolog's most extensive description = Maniacky 2003 (a wordlist or less); also cites Fleisch 2000: 13 ('Comments on subclassification').
sources.note: Nothing; it lists only one comparative/overview reference (Maniacky 2003, pp. 208-223) and a one-page classification comment in Fleisch 2000 — no grammar, sketch or phonology exists for nkan1238 in Glottolog.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en), 'Nkangala language' (redirects to 'Mbunda language'), accessed 2026-09-17; cites Maniacky 1997, 'Contribution à l'étude des langues bantoues de la zone K: analyse comparative et sous-groupements', via bantu-languages.com.
sources.note: Treats Nkangala as one of several Mbunda dialects; the 'Sounds' section gives Mbunda vowels/consonants only, nothing on tone, accent or stress for any variety.

sources.citation: Ethnologue, 17th ed. (Lewis, Simons & Fennig 2014), entry Nkangala [nkn], via the Internet Archive capture.
sources.note: Nothing on phonology. Gives 22,300 speakers (2000); Kwando, Kubango and Moxico provinces, SW of Lucazi, N of Mbwela; classification K, Ciokwe-Luchazi (K.18); 'Dialects: None known. Member of Ngangela cluster. Intelligible with Nyemba [nba], Mbwela [mfu], Ngonzela, and Lucazi [lch].'

sources.citation: Zavoni, Ntondo. 2003. Éléments de description du ngangela. Thèse de doctorat, Université Lumière Lyon 2. Chapitre I Phonologie (Kuvango variety) — already held by the project for nyem1238.
sources.note: Its accent-vs-tone discussion (pp. 82-83) concerns the Kuvango variety of Ngangela (catalogued under nyem1238); a full-text search for stress/accent/'Kangala' in the text returns nothing, so it says nothing about Nkangala.

sources.note: Glottolog's Glottolog's most extensive description for Mbunda (mbun1249); if Nkangala is a Mbunda dialect (Wikipedia/Maniacky 1997), this sketch's phonology section is the nearest existing description of its prosody.

sources.citation: Fleisch, Axel. 2009. Language history in SE Angola: the Ngangela-Nyemba dialect cluster. In Wilhelm J.G. Möhlig, Frank Seidel & Marc Seifert (eds.), Language Contact, Language Change and History Based on Language Sources in Africa (SUGIA 20), 385 pp. Köln: Rüdiger Köppe. ISBN 978-3-89645-093-7. (Earlier version: Fleisch 2008, SUGIA 19.)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Comparative-historical dialect-cluster study; the only modern treatment of the whole Ngangela-Nyemba cluster (which contains Nkangala). A cluster study by the author of the Lucazi grammar may report the prosodic/tonal profile of each variety and the status of Nkangala.

sources.citation: Maniacky, Jacky. 2003. Variétés du Ngangela. In Jacky Maniacky, Tonologie du ngangela: variété de Menongue (Angola), 208-223. LINCOM Studies in African Linguistics 61. München: LINCOM. ISBN 9783895868009.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: The only work Glottolog ties to Nkangala [nkn] (listed by Glottolog as an overview/comparative; language code includes Nkangala). It sits inside a tonology monograph whose blurb promises comparisons 'avec les autres variétés ngangela', so it is the likeliest place for any first-hand remark on tone/accent in the Nkangala variety; it would also settle whether Nkangala shares the Menongue 'restricted tone, accent-like' system.

sources.citation: Fleisch, Axel. 2000. Lucazi Grammar: a morphosemantic analysis. Grammatische Analysen Afrikanischer Sprachen 15. Köln: Rüdiger Köppe. 363 pp. ISBN 9783896450388.

sources.note: Glottolog cites p. 13 ('Comments on subclassification') for Nkangala; the closest full grammar of a cluster sister (Luchazi, which Ethnologue lists as mutually intelligible with Nkangala) with a phonology chapter — useful for the identity question and as the nearest description of the cluster's prosody, but not a Nkangala description.

sources.citation: Maniacky, Jacky. 1997. Contribution à l'étude des langues bantoues de la zone K: analyse comparative et sous-groupements. Mémoire, INALCO, Paris.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Comparative subgrouping study cited (via bantu-languages.com) as the basis for treating Nkangala as a dialect of Mbunda; needed to resolve the identity of nkan1238 (separate language per Glottolog/Ethnologue vs Mbunda dialect) before any Mbunda or Ngangela statement could be transferred.

sources.note: Locally produced Ngangela grammar from Menongue (Cuando Cubango), listed in Maniacky's K12b bibliography; it might name the varieties covered (Nkangala speakers are in Kubango province) and give an orthographic/prosodic note, but it is otherwise unlocated.
